result.title: KALEIDO: Input-Space Adaptation of a Vision Model for Time-Series Forecasting Through Gated Fold Geometries
result.comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Foundation Models for Temporal Systems (FMTS)
result.summary: Time-series foundation models buy zero-shot forecasting with large temporal corpora; a vision model needs none, since a natural image implicitly embeds the patterns a forecaster must model, and an ImageNet-pretrained masked autoencoder forecasts a series by inpainting a rendering of it. A rendered series is not a natural image, however, and closing that gap takes temporal-aware adaptation. We show that the rendering geometry - how the series is folded and drawn - is a controllable, mixable axis for it. Kaleido detects the dominant periods, renders a rule-generated set of fold geometries, combines the inpaintings with a convex per-position gate fit on validation only, and fuses the result with the zero-shot output at one fixed share, with no per-dataset hyperparameter beyond the baseline's published settings. Training only LayerNorm (0.05%), Kaleido lowers MSE by 13% against the published zero-shot baseline on LTSF and, frozen, by 6.6%; on GIFT-Eval it improves the baseline by 7.4% in MASE and 19.3% in CRPS.

AI.brief_summary: KALEIDO 将时间序列按检测到的主周期折叠渲染成图像，用 ImageNet 预训练 MAE 做 inpainting 预测，并通过凸门控组合多种折叠几何、与零样本输出融合，仅训练 LayerNorm 即提升预测指标。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽属时间序列预测，但其「输入被渲染成何种几何/表示决定模型能否抽取必要信息」与 LVR 关注的视觉细节、任务必要信息是否保留在内部状态、以及视觉旁路与信息坍缩问题可能相通，可供核查表示几何与门控融合是否可迁移到 latent 状态的证据筛选。
